text:
The output offset is caused by a badly unbalanced differential pair. The load mirror M3/M4 has a 6.67× current ratio (W 26.3/3.945, and the measured currents 21.6 µA vs 3.24 µA match it), so M2 carries about 7× more current than M1. That mismatch in Vgs (0.605 V vs 0.695 V, with a shared source at about 0.205 V) produces roughly 90 mV of input-referred offset. A balanced 1:1 load would split the 24.8 µA tail roughly evenly. M4 has the largest offset sensitivity (+8.84%) and also drives the bandwidth loss (-10.9%), so its width is the most likely corruption. M3 and M5 are the next candidates: M3 is the other half of the mirror ratio, and M5 is in triode, which lowers the tail current and reduces bandwidth.

This creates about -90 mV input-referred offset (vout_offset -0.091 V) and reduces the bandwidth of the input stage. Restoring a 1:1 mirror (M4 W equal to M3 W, or M3 at 26.3 um) should balance the pair and fix the offset; M5 being in triode is a downstream symptom to recheck afterward."}
